newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers meet on post-EMU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers meet on post-EMU budget pact.

text.p: European Union finance ministers began meeting on Monday to try to agree a new system for ensuring that countries in a single currency maintain the budgetary discipline required after joining.
Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn, who will chair the meeting, said he expected the ministers to advance their plans, but was not sure whether an agreement could be reached.
"We'll make some progress but how far we get remains to be seen. All the indicatiosn are very positive," Quinn said as he arrived for the meeting.
Earlier, Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said chances of reaching an agreement were better than advertised.
"The situation is better than expected," he said.
The effort to secure a so-called budget stability pact has become one of the most difficult hurdles in nailing down a blueprint for economic and monetary union (EMU).
Under a proposed plan, countries running annual deficits above three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) could face stiff fines if they failed to curb expenditure.
But if a government could show that a severe recession was behind the deterioration of its public finances, it might be able to avoid sanctions.

Germany wants the recession defined as a two percent annual decline in GDP. Others have argued for a less rigid approach, preferring a range -- a fall in output of between 0.5 and 2.0 percent -- that would force EU finance ministers to decide whether fines were appropriate.

If finance ministers do not agree on Monday, it is likely that EU leaders meeting at a summit in Dublin on December 13 will be able to agree only an outline of a plan, leaving a firm decision until the next summit, in June.
